purpose: Track when overall transport performance deteriorates and how much it recovers without generating a synthetic disaster trajectory.
required_data: two or more observed time points

mathematical_formulation.service: q_t = mean_i min(1, v_it / v_i_ref) for speed; q_t = mean_i min(1, tau_i_ref / tau_it) for travel time

performance: Trapezoidal integration over adjacent uploaded intervals; gaps longer than 1.5 times the median interval are excluded.
verification_contract: large gaps receive zero integration weight

primary_sources.citation: Faturechi and Miller-Hooks (2015), Measuring the performance of transportation infrastructure systems in disasters: a comprehensive review, Journal of Infrastructure Systems.
primary_sources.relationship: Resilience performance framing; the Transport World Model platform implements a narrower observed-data integral.

known_limitations: The internal reference is not automatically pre-disaster.
The curve is descriptive and not a causal no-disaster counterfactual.
A primary hazard metric has no universal service direction and is therefore not accepted by this model.
